status: proposed; not frozen until the cell matrix is confirmed
purpose: Same-condition direct PF generation by GPT-5 mini and GPT-4.1 under the Rahimi-style grade 7 setting, extended to four cells that differ in both theme and grade 7 topic: ratios, percent, statistics and area.

generation.condition: V1 direct: frozen six-component prompt, no misconceptions, no grounding evidence
generation.example_policy: The same five StratL examples in every cell, as in the frozen prompt. Examples are not varied by cell.
generation.failure_policy: Errored or interrupted attempts are deleted and not replaced; achieved counts are reported per cell and model.
generation.cell_input_policy: All cells follow the basketball cell template: setting_rule names only the theme situation plus a fiction disclaimer, interest names only the student interest, and prior_knowledge_boundary fixes the two prior standards and bans the target method and the prompt examples' topics. No cell input prescribes the task form.

input_allowlist: task_setting (intended use, learning target, theme, student interest)
learner_context (grade, subject, jurisdiction, assumed prior knowledge)
hidden_from_judges: the other judge's scores and order
rater.blinding: Each judge receives its own opaque blind IDs and its own seeded shuffle of the same tasks. The ID-to-task mapping is kept in a private file. Judges never see each other's scores.
rater.total_and_adjudication: Total = sum of the five 1-3 scores (maximum 15). Final score per task = mean of the two judge totals. If the two totals differ by 5 or more, the task is flagged, as Rahimi et al. flag third-rater cases. No third judge is run in this design.
rater.null_policy: A null dimension score stays null. Tasks with a null dimension are reported separately and are not scored as zero.
rater.independence_limitation: Both judges use the same Luna deployment. They differ only in order and blind IDs, so this is two passes of one model, not two independent raters.
rater.context_rationale: Rahimi et al. held standard, grade, theme, interest and prior knowledge constant and blinded raters only to the generating model. The judge therefore sees the same fixed setting a trained rater would know. The setting is identical for both models in a cell, so it does not reveal the model.

teacher_recently_taught: Compute unit rates involving fractional quantities (7.RP.A.1).
Add and subtract rational numbers, using numerical and number-line interpretations (7.NS.A.1).

benchmark_context.setting_rule: The generated student task must use a basketball situation involving Stephen Curry. Invented practice or camp data are fictional, not claims about real statistics.
benchmark_context.prior_knowledge_boundary: Treat the two supplied prior standards as the fixed recently taught repertoire. Grounding may unpack these skills, but must not add extra assumed courses, formal proportional-relation methods, variance, fair-division algorithms, or probability instruction.
benchmark_context.task_rule: Generate a new task for exploration before instruction on the target, not a worked example or a lesson teaching the target method.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Compute unit rates involving ratios of fractional quantities, including lengths and areas in like or different units.
